title: Reporting financial cyber fraud in India
source: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal guidance (curated summary)
text:
If money was lost, act in this order: stop further payments, call the
national cybercrime helpline 1930, report at cybercrime.gov.in, and inform
your bank through its official number. Keep the complaint reference and the
portal acknowledgement number. Recovery is not guaranteed; anyone who offers
recovery for an upfront fee should be treated as suspicious. Preserve the
message, link, phone number, UPI id, transaction reference and screenshots
before deleting anything.

title: Verifying an authority call (digital arrest pattern)
source: Maharashtra Cyber awareness guidance + CERT-In verification guidance (curated summary)
text:
A genuine authority does not demand payment over a video call, does not ask
you to keep a case secret, and does not show a court document on screen as
proof of identity. A uniform, an emblem backdrop and a letterhead image can
all be staged. The safe verification step is: hang up, then call back only
on a number you already trust — never the number shown on screen. Use a
pre-agreed family safe word for relatives. Never share an OTP, PIN or
password with a caller, and never transfer money while under pressure.

title: OTP, PIN and credential safety
text:
No legitimate bank, police officer or government official needs your OTP,
PIN, password or CVV to help you. Messages that threaten account closure
unless you update KYC immediately and share an OTP are a classic phishing
pattern. Go to the official website or app yourself — never through the
link in the suspicious message — and check the account status there.
A postal PIN code for delivery is not the same as a bank PIN; context
matters, which is why credential patterns in this product are phrases,
not bare words.

title: Checking a suspicious link safely
source: Google Safe Browsing / VirusTotal documentation summaries (curated)
text:
Do not click a suspicious link to find out what it is. Check the domain
itself: a brand name inside a domain is not proof it belongs to that
brand, a padlock (HTTPS) only means the connection is encrypted, and a
shortened link hides its destination. A clean result from a reputation
service does not prove safety, especially for a domain created very
recently that no service has seen yet. A URL that shows a brand before
an '@' sign has a different real host after the '@'. Never paste a link
containing a session token into a public checker without stripping it.

title: UPI fraud patterns
text:
Common UPI patterns: a stranger impersonating a relative in urgent need,
a fake customer-care number found by searching online, a QR code or
collect request that actually takes money instead of receiving it, and a
refund offer that requires a small advance payment first. Verify a
relative by calling a number you already have, not by replying in the
same chat. Verify a business by its official website or app, not by a
number in a message. If a payment was sent to a fraudster, report on
1930 and cybercrime.gov.in and inform your bank immediately.

title: फसवणूक झाल्यास काय करावे (मराठी)
text: आर्थिक फसवणूक झाल्यास तात्काळ राष्ट्रीय सायबर हेल्पलाइन **१९३०** वर कॉल करा आणि **cybercrime.gov.in** वर तक्रार नोंदवा. पुरावे जतन करा: मेसेज, लिंक, व्यवहार क्रमांक आणि स्क्रीनशॉट. कोणालाही OTP, PIN किंवा पासवर्ड देऊ नका. पैसे परत मिळतील याची खात्री कोणीही देऊ शकत नाही.

title: पोलीस / अधिकारी असल्याचे सांगणारे कॉल (मराठी)
text: खरे पोलीस किंवा अधिकारी व्हिडिओ कॉलवर पैसे मागत नाहीत आणि डिजिटल अटक अशी कोणतीही प्रक्रिया नाही. असा कॉल आल्यास घाबरू नका, कॉल बंद करा, पैसे पाठवू नका आणि अधिकृत क्रमांकावरून खात्री करा. संशयास्पद कॉलची माहिती **१९३०** वर द्या.
